body_markdown:
*New Section 232 tariffs make the communications technology you integrate today a supply-chain, compliance and procurement decision, not only a cost decision.*


**


**


The U.S. defense market is raising the bar for UAS readiness. For manufacturers of unmanned and autonomous platforms, the choice of communications technology now shapes more than performance. It affects supply-chain predictability, compliance, procurement and, ultimately, the path to deployment.


**Section 232: A New Baseline for the U.S. Market**


On August 13, 2026, President Donald J. Trump signed a proclamation imposing tariffs of up to 100% on certain foreign drones and critical components, to bolster domestic supply chains and reduce foreign cybersecurity risks. The new Section 232 tariffs took effect on September 3, 2026. The framework offers incentives for U.S. manufacturing investments and provides delayed tariff effective dates for qualifying products on the U.S. Department of War’s FCC Trusted Drone Approval list. For details, see the official[White House proclamation](https://www.whitehouse.gov/presidential-actions/2026/08/adjusting-imports-of-unmanned-aircraft-systems-and-unmanned-aircraft-systems-components-into-the-united-states/) .


For UAS and autonomous platform manufacturers, this goes beyond cost. The communications technology you integrate today can impact supply-chain predictability, compliance, procurement and, ultimately, your path to deployment. That makes U.S. readiness an increasingly important part of the technology decision.


****


**U.S. Readiness Starts with the Communications Layer**


Mobilicom has already advanced several strategic initiatives aligned with the new framework:


- **FCC Trusted Drone status:** Mobilicom’s solutions, including SkyHopper datalinks, ground control stations, ICE electronic warfare resistance, and OS3 cybersecurity software, were[named to the FCC’s initial Trusted Drones list](https://mobilicom.com/news-updates/?y=2026) , backed by an approved U.S. onshoring roadmap.
- **NDAA and U.S. defense compliance:** Validated under NDAA standards, the Blue UAS Framework, AUVSI Trusted Cyber, and DD1494 qualifications, Mobilicom provides a fully compliant component ecosystem for manufacturers transitioning away from foreign technologies.
- **U.S. onshore manufacturing buildout:** As outlined in the company’s first-half 2026 earnings call, Mobilicom is advancing its U.S. onshore manufacturing initiatives and remains on track to support anticipated domestic customer demand.


“We welcome President Trump’s actions to secure America’s drone supply chains and accelerate domestic production,” said Oren Elkayam, Founder and CEO of Mobilicom. “Our multi-year strategy and targeted investments to establish Mobilicom as a validated U.S. defense technology supplier are now positioning us to capitalize on emerging opportunities in the U.S. market.”[Read the full announcement](https://www.globenewswire.com/news-release/2026/08/17/3345973/0/en/mobilicom-is-set-for-this-moment-positioned-to-capture-growing-u-s-market-demand-following-new-federal-tariff-policy.html) .


****


**Building for U.S. Deployment**


With FCC Trusted Drone status, NDAA and U.S. defense compliance, and a U.S. onshore manufacturing buildout underway, Mobilicom is positioned to help customers reduce integration and security risk while supporting deployment into U.S. defense programs.
